To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

lead retention in suckling and in adult female mice is independent of the dose of lead administered, but that the fraction of the dose that is retained and the organ lead concentrations are developmentally regulated.

the FID retained by both suckling and mature mice is dose independent, and that developmental differences in FID retained and in the distribution of lead in organs are observed following an acute lead administration.

the fraction of initial lead dose retained is dose-independent, but developmental differences exist in this fraction for suckling and adult females; that the relationship of blood to organ lead concentrations is nonlinear; that lead concentrations of blood are good indicators of kidney and liver concentrations; and that the relationship between blood and bone lead concentrations is nonlinear.

the effects of dose on lead absorption, retention, and distribution in sucklings and adults.
the development of a model to describe lead kinetics and the effects of dose on lead distribution and retention.
the effects of lead dose and developmental differences on the absorption, retention, and distribution of lead.
